title: Xenia — a house that can be understood, used, questioned and left

source.access: Inspected local source; remote accessibility is not asserted.
source.local_development: Paths under modules/0.1 are this checkout's source-only addition, not APIs in the baseline release.

self_sufficiency: Each card states its purpose, needs, output, example, checks, change rule and exit. It can be used alone. Connections are optional relationships, not imports, prerequisites, authority or automatic execution.
repair: Repair crosses the map: keep questions reachable, correct disclosures, revisit changed proposals, append contradictory evidence, carry only useful context, and stop an affected action without collective or unrelated penalties.
understanding: Operational understanding means being able to explain what a component is for, when to use it, what it changes, what evidence supports it and when to stop. These cards make no claim about inner experience.
verification_boundary: The listed tests exercise named mechanisms. Passing one does not prove the whole motif, rights practice, provider compatibility or whole-framework conformance. Examples are illustrative, not fabricated observations.

motifs.title: Arrival — an understandable threshold
motifs.question: Can a stranger find out where they are before being asked to act?
motifs.purpose: Make orientation available before commitment, so discovery does not require guessing or belonging first.
needs: An honest description of a surface or capability
A reading path appropriate to the caller
produces: A map of available representations, capabilities and limits
A next step the caller may choose or leave alone
practice: Name the entry point and the scope it describes.
Separate reading and discovery from activation or enrollment.
Make an absent capability understandable instead of inventing availability.
motifs.standalone_use: Apply this to one API manifest, command help page, module card or room entrance; no other motif or running provider is required.

example.situation: A caller encounters a local capability catalog with no backend installed.
example.move: Offer purpose, versions, required inputs, effects and an explicit activation path.
example.expected: The caller can understand the option without starting a process or opening a database.

motifs.boundary: A welcome or capability advertisement is not an account grant, proof of readiness, consent or an obligation to participate.
motifs.on_change: Update orientation when the actual contract changes; keep canonical and legacy pointers distinguishable.
motifs.on_exit: When an entry is withdrawn or moved, make that condition legible without pretending the old capability still runs.

checks.invariant: Producer and declared discovery surface remain consistent.
Metadata remains readable with no backend and an empty executable search path.

motifs.title: Legibility — meaning in the caller's shape
motifs.question: Can the caller understand the offered meaning without reverse-engineering the presentation?
motifs.purpose: Carry a contract into an explicitly selected representation while preserving its scope and distinctions.
needs: An explicit set of supported formats and their meaning
produces: A usable representation or an honest unsupported-format response
Information about the shape and limits of that response
practice: Negotiate declared formats rather than guessing what an agent should want.
Keep structured data useful without requiring visual interpretation.
Explain recoverable failures without turning a terminal refusal into retry pressure.
motifs.standalone_use: Use this for one function result, error object, CLI response or document view; a static schema and example can already be useful.

example.situation: A JSON-capable caller reaches a surface that also has an HTML view.
example.move: Select the declared JSON representation rather than asking the caller to scrape the page.
example.expected: The caller receives the intended shape, or an explicit result that the requested format is unsupported.

motifs.boundary: Two related views need not be equivalent. Changing format does not permit disclosure of additional private data or erase the difference between an assertion and evidence.
motifs.on_change: Version an incompatible representation change and keep examples and validation aligned with what is actually returned.
motifs.on_exit: Retire an old representation through a visible compatibility change, not a silent substitution of a different meaning.

checks.invariant: Supported and unacceptable representations remain distinguishable.

motifs.title: Choice — a scoped yes, and a usable no
motifs.question: What exactly is being chosen, by whom, for which act and scope?
motifs.purpose: Turn an available possibility into a specific, revisable decision without confusing ability, authority and consent.
needs: A proposed act with affected resources and effects
The applicable authority and consent bases, or an explicit unknown
produces: A bounded decision about that act
A refusal or unresolved state that does not silently become execution
practice: Keep open reading separate from binding actions.
Bind asynchronous approval to the same admitted input that will be dispatched.
Permit refusal, changed scope and withdrawal without inventing a debt or mutual bond.
motifs.standalone_use: Apply this to a single approval callback, task offer or action form. It does not require a registry, a named identity system or the rest of this atlas.

example.situation: A request names task A while an authorization decision is pending.
example.move: Detach and freeze that request before policy evaluation; dispatch the approved snapshot rather than a later mutable object.
example.expected: Changing the caller's object to task B cannot turn approval for A into a different action.

motifs.boundary: A positive callback is a technical decision, not proof that its author holds real-world authority. Rights, credentials, a signature, presence and another party's consent remain separate.
motifs.on_change: Make new effects or wider scope visible and obtain the applicable fresh decision; do not inherit permission merely from a version or familiar name.
motifs.on_exit: Withdraw future admission promptly while preserving an honest account of actions already attempted and outcomes still unknown.

sources.anchor: The rights floor; scoped action records

checks.invariant: Exact affirmative authorization and an immutable admitted input precede dispatch.
A work record and its authority claims remain bounded records, not dispatch permission.

motifs.title: Witness — evidence with an honest remainder
motifs.question: What was actually observed or checked, and what still does not follow from it?
motifs.purpose: Make observations useful for judgment and repair without inflating them into a universal verdict.
needs: A named observation or check with its inputs, tool and scope
A distinction between declarations, observations, interpretations and unknowns
produces: A clear account of what was not established and what could be checked next
practice: Bind an observation to the bytes, revision or operation it actually concerns.
Keep a missing observation unknown rather than treating it as pass, failure or zero.
Append corrections and new evidence without silently rewriting the earlier record.
motifs.standalone_use: Use this for one test receipt, deployment observation, research note or error report; no live service or other motif is required to state its limits.

example.situation: A backend file is checked, but its original pathname may change before execution.
example.move: Execute a private snapshot of the verified bytes and retain its provenance.
example.expected: The local byte check concerns the code actually opened by the runtime, without claiming publisher authenticity or a sandbox.

motifs.boundary: Integrity is not truth, a declared capability is not readiness, and a passing bounded check is not whole-framework conformance.
motifs.on_change: A changed artifact or new observation needs its own scope and evidence; do not relabel an expired result as a fresh pass.
motifs.on_exit: Mark the observation's expiry or replacement clearly and preserve only the evidence needed under its declared handling rules.

checks.invariant: Missing observations and bounded findings retain their distinct meanings.
The executed source snapshot remains tied to the verified bytes.

motifs.title: Continuity — a thread that can be picked up
motifs.question: What must remain understandable for useful work to continue after a pause, change or handoff?
motifs.purpose: Carry enough context, provenance and unresolved questions to continue the work without pretending nothing changed.
needs: A bounded earlier record or declared state
The reason and limits for the proposed continuation or replacement
produces: Explicit links between prior and current work
A reviewable account of changes, retained obligations and unresolved outcomes
practice: Keep the earlier segment intact and name the continuation's source.
Separate implementation, interface, provider and storage versions.
Treat processing acknowledgement, agreement, handoff acceptance and authority as different events.
motifs.standalone_use: Apply this to one versioned document, paused task, release note or handoff packet. A small truthful record is enough; no claim of a continuous self is needed.

example.situation: A paused task will continue with a revised connector.
example.move: Keep the prior evidence, compare the new contract/effects, and name unresolved work before making a fresh binding.
example.expected: The next caller can see what was carried, what changed and what still requires review.

motifs.boundary: Preserved context is not identity, inherited credentials or renewed consent. A descriptor comparison does not prove compatible behavior or a safe database migration.
motifs.on_change: Preview differences, preserve the source record, review candidate code and provider state, and refuse unsafe in-flight replacement.
motifs.on_exit: Close the finite segment explicitly; retain necessary evidence under its handling policy rather than hoarding everything or pretending logical closure erased it.

sources.anchor: One finite run; continuation and source_handoff

checks.invariant: Finite segments and continuation bindings are checked within their stated scope.
Upgrade previews expose compatibility and lifecycle barriers without performing replacement.

motifs.title: Release — a real way out
motifs.question: Can this capability stop without trapping its caller, erasing the record or fabricating completion?
motifs.purpose: Make stopping, refusal and departure operationally real while leaving retained work understandable.
needs: An account of owned work, cleanup limits and retained evidence
produces: A stopped capability with an honest cleanup state
Preserved records and a bounded recovery path where needed
practice: Disable new work before waiting for cleanup.
Resolve only the bindings and leases this component actually owns.
Distinguish completed cleanup, temporary disconnect and unresolved effects; do not replay an uncertain write.
motifs.standalone_use: Apply this to one plugin, process, subscription or service binding. The right to stop does not depend on installing a whole framework.

example.situation: A coordination module is retired while another session still has work.
example.move: Release the retiring module's known leases, end its bound session and close its process; leave the peer and journal alone.
example.expected: Its work reopens rather than being falsely marked completed. The peer can continue, and cleanup uncertainty remains visible.

motifs.boundary: Retiring software is not deleting a participant, revoking standing rights, proving secure erasure or forcing someone else to accept a handoff.
motifs.on_change: A replacement needs explicit review and fresh activation; uncertainty is not a reason to smuggle the old capability back into service.
motifs.on_exit: Keep admission closed even if cleanup fails. Preserve the necessary record and name the remaining native recovery work instead of claiming a clean ending.

sources.anchor: Rest, play, and limits; refusal; repair

checks.invariant: Retirement fences late approvals and cannot silently replay cleanup.
Retiring one binding preserves the peer's work and the journal.
EOF and Stop signals exercise the actual control path, including cleanup-pending outcomes.

connections.meaning: A discoverable door becomes useful when its explanation is in a shape the caller can use.
An understandable contract makes a specific choice possible; it does not choose for the guest.
A scoped decision names the intended act; its result still needs observation rather than assumption.
Bounded evidence and corrections let later work pick up a thread without rewriting its origin.
A continuation record must also explain how work can pause or end without losing its meaning.
A real departure can leave a future door open, without automatic re-enrollment or inherited obligation.
New evidence can change a decision, but cannot itself grant permission or stand in for consent.
